newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FORECAST - Bulgaria GDP to fall 8.1-10.5 pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Bulgaria GDP to fall 8.1-10.5 pct in '96.

text.p: Bulgaria's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to fall by between 8.1 percent and 10.5 percent this year and by 2.0 to 4.0 percent in 1997, a National Statistics Institute (NSI) forecast said.

"A GDP fall by a real eight percent for this year could be considered a realistic forecast while a 10.5 percent fall could be expected under more unfavourable economic conditions in the fourth quarter," the NSI said.

GDP fell by a real 6.2 percent year on year in the first half of 1996 to 493 billion levs at current prices, the NSI said. This compared to a 2.4 percent rise for the first six months of 1995 to 330.9 billion levs at current prices.

Annual inflation for 1996 was assumed at 230-240 percent in the forecast, which meant that monthly inflation should average 10 percent in the fourth quarter after cumulative inflation for the first nine months totalled 153 percent, the NSI said.
"Monthly inflation of some 10 percent, a fairly stable lev/dollar exchange rate and no drastic rises in interest rates or energy prices were assumed in the 1996 forecast," the NSI said.
GDP could be expected to fall by some two to four percent next year to 3,500-3,900 billion levs at current prices if the economic environment changes for the better, the NSI said.

Annual inflation of 60-70 percent, a stabilisation of the country's shaky financial system, a moderate lev fall against major currencies and a rising share of the private sector were assumed in the 1997 forecast.

The central government budget revision made in July forecast zero GDP growth this year, down from an originally planned three percent, annual consumer price inflation of 100 percent and an average annual central interest rate of 68 percent.
However, huge domestic debt burdens and a banking crisis had pushed the annual interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent last month, which was cut to 240 percent 10 days ago.

The budget deficit overshot the annual target by 5.4 percent in mid-October, rising to 85.1 billion levs while state industrial output fell by 12 percent year-on-year in September due to high interest rates and a fall in orders.
The deficit was assumed at 4.9 percent of gross domestic product or 80.7 billion levs in the revised budget, to be mostly funded by the central bank through government securities purchases.

The projected lev/dollar exchange rate of 190 was also topped as the lev traded near 240 to the dollar on Tuesday and was expected to weaken further due to low foreign exchange reserves and uncertainty over foreign funding.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) twice delayed the second $115 million tranche of a standby agreement sealed in July until the Socialist government closes down loss-makers and speeds up privatisation.
